indications.label: Neurology
indications.note: B6 dependent seizures. High dose trial.

indications.label: Cardiovascular
indications.note: Calcium channel bl. Do not crush.

indications.label: Endocrine
indications.note: Not for <10 yrs. Lactic acidosis risk.

indications.label: Supplements
indications.note: High dose prophylaxis. Do not exceed.

indications.label: Hemato-Oncology
indications.note: Neurotoxicity risk. FATAL if given intrathecally.

indications.label: Hemato-Oncology
indications.note: Cardiotoxicity risk. Lifetime dose limits apply.

indications.label: Neonatal Infection
indications.note: AUDIT: Dose aligns with BNFc. Adjust for renal impairment in neonates.

indications.label: Pediatric Bacterial Infection
indications.note: AUDIT: Max daily dose typically capped at 300mg/kg or 4g/day in standard practice.

indications.label: Meningitis
indications.note: AUDIT: Higher CNS penetration doses used; monitor CSF clearance.

indications.label: Gram-negative/Pseudomonas Infection
indications.note: AUDIT: Neonates <4 weeks require extended interval (q12-24h). Monitor renal function.

indications.label: Serious Gram-negative Infection
indications.note: AUDIT: High nephro/ototoxicity risk. TDM mandatory (peak/trough). Avoid prolonged use >7 days without review.

indications.label: Fever/Pain
indications.note: AUDIT: Unit corrected to mg/kg/day in standard literature. Max 4 doses/24h. Hepatic toxicity risk if exceeded.

indications.label: GERD/Peptic Ulcer
indications.note: AUDIT: Off-label in children <12 months. Omeprazole or Pantoprazole preferred in peds. Capsule not crushable.

indications.label: Severe/Resistant Bacterial Infection
indications.note: AUDIT: Meningitis dose 40mg/kg/dose q8h. Reserve for ESBL/resistant pathogens. Infuse over 15-30 min.

indications.label: Broad-spectrum Infection/Meningitis
indications.note: AUDIT: CONTRAINDICATED in neonates with hyperbilirubinemia or calcium-containing IV fluids (precipitation risk).

indications.label: Gram-negative Sepsis
indications.note: AUDIT: Extended interval dosing preferred. TDM essential. Avoid with other nephrotoxins.

indications.label: Complicated UTI/Typhoid
indications.note: AUDIT: Off-label <18y. Cartilage toxicity risk. Reserve for MDR pathogens or when alternatives fail.

indications.label: Anaerobic/Amebic Infection
indications.note: AUDIT: Avoid in neonates <4 weeks (immature hepatic clearance). Risk of peripheral neuropathy with prolonged use.

indications.label: Edema/Heart Failure/Nephrotic Syndrome
indications.note: AUDIT: Monitor K+, Na+, creatinine. IV infusion rate <4mg/min to avoid ototoxicity.

indications.label: Respiratory/ENT Infections
indications.note: AUDIT: High-dose (45-90mg/kg/day) recommended for otitis media/pneumococcal resistance. Reconstitute properly.

indications.label: Metabolic Acidosis/Cardiac Arrest
indications.note: AUDIT: Must dilute for peripheral IV. Administer slowly. Correct underlying cause first. Monitor ABGs.

indications.label: Status Asthmaticus/Apnea of Prematurity
indications.note: AUDIT: Narrow therapeutic index (10-20 mcg/ml). High seizure/arrhythmia risk. Largely replaced by β2-agonists/steroids.

indications.label: Hemodynamic Support/Shock
indications.note: AUDIT: Titrate to BP/urine output. Extravasation causes tissue necrosis. Prefer central line.

indications.label: Acute Asthma/Bronchospasm
indications.note: AUDIT: Monitor HR, K+, tremor. Nebulizer preferred over syrup for acute distress.

indications.label: Acute Bronchospasm/COPD
indications.note: AUDIT: <6 months: 250mcg. >6 months: 500mcg. Synergistic with salbutamol.

indications.label: Croup/Asthma Maintenance
indications.frequency: Once daily (croup: up to 2mg single dose)
indications.note: AUDIT: Rinse mouth post-use if possible. Not for acute bronchodilation; reduces mucosal edema.

indications.label: Febrile/Status Convulsions
indications.note: AUDIT: Rapid IV push causes apnea/hypotension. PR absorption delayed. Lorazepam preferred if available.

indications.label: Neonatal Seizures
indications.frequency: Loading IV over 20 min, then 3-5mg/kg/day maintenance
indications.note: AUDIT: First-line for neonates. Monitor levels (15-40 mcg/ml). Long half-life; accumulation risk.

indications.label: Status Epilepticus
indications.frequency: Loading IV over 10-15 min, then 4-5mg PE/kg/day
indications.note: AUDIT: Dilute only in NS or D5W. Monitor BP/ECG during infusion. Less tissue injury than phenytoin.

indications.label: Seizures/Sedation
indications.note: AUDIT: Rapid onset. High apnea risk in neonates/premature. Requires resuscitation equipment nearby.

indications.label: Focal/Generalized Seizures
indications.note: AUDIT: Well-tolerated, minimal drug interactions. TDM rarely required. Adjust for renal impairment.

indications.label: Atypical Pneumonia/Pharyngitis
indications.note: AUDIT: Prolonged QT risk. Avoid with macrolide-sensitive strains. Convenient once-daily dosing.

indications.label: Acute Diarrhea
indications.note: AUDIT: Enkephalinase inhibitor; reduces stool output. Adjunct to ORS/Zinc. Avoid if bloody diarrhea/fever.

indications.label: Acute Diarrhea
indications.note: AUDIT: WHO standard. <6 months: 10mg/day. Reduce vomiting/duration. Give after food to avoid nausea.

indications.label: Nephrotic Syndrome/Severe Asthma
indications.note: AUDIT: Taper slowly to avoid adrenal crisis. Monitor BP, glucose, growth velocity. Give with food.

indications.label: Heart Failure/Hypertension
indications.note: AUDIT: Start low, titrate slowly. Monitor K+, creatinine, BP. Risk of first-dose hypotension.

indications.label: Envenomation (Neurotoxic/Vasculotoxic)
indications.frequency: IV over 1 hour, repeat if needed
indications.note: AUDIT: High anaphylaxis risk. Pre-medicate with antihistamine/steroids. Monitor vitals closely during infusion.

indications.label: Septic Shock/Croup/Allergic Reaction
indications.note: AUDIT: IV push or infusion. Stress-dose steroids for refractory shock. Monitor glucose/K+.

indications.label: Croup/Meningitis Adjunct
indications.note: AUDIT: Preferred for croup (single dose). In bacterial meningitis, give before/with first antibiotic dose.

indications.label: HSV/VZV Encephalitis
indications.note: AUDIT: Neonatal dose: 20mg/kg/dose q8h. Ensure IV hydration to prevent crystalluria. Infuse >1 hour.

indications.label: GERD/Peptic Ulcer Prophylaxis
indications.note: AUDIT: Off-label <1 month. IV infusion rate ≤25mg/min. Consider PPIs (omeprazole) as first-line per BNFc 2024.

indications.label: Acute Moderate-Severe Pain
indications.note: AUDIT: CONTRAINDICATED <6 months. Max duration 5 days (renal/GI risk). Avoid with other NSAIDs/anticoagulants. Not for minor pain.

indications.label: Chemotherapy-Induced/Post-Op Nausea
indications.note: AUDIT: Off-label <6 months for gastroenteritis. QT prolongation risk—avoid with other QT-prolonging drugs. IV infusion over ≥15 min.

indications.label: UTI/Otitis Media/Pharyngitis
indications.note: AUDIT: Not for neonates. Reserve for β-lactam resistant cases. Complete full course to prevent resistance. Reconstitute syrup properly.

indications.label: UTI/PJP Prophylaxis/Shigella
indications.note: AUDIT: CONTRAINDICATED <6 weeks (kernicterus risk). Monitor CBC/LFTs. High hypersensitivity risk—discontinue if rash. PJP dose: 20mg TMP/kg/day.

indications.label: Allergic Reaction/Urticaria
indications.note: AUDIT: Sedating—caution in respiratory depression. IV infusion rate ≤1mg/min. Prefer non-sedating antihistamines (cetirizine) for daytime use per BNFc.

indications.label: Neonatal Hemorrhagic Disease Prophylaxis
indications.note: AUDIT: Standard WHO/UNICEF protocol. Preterm <1.5kg: 0.5mg. IV use only for active bleeding (slow infusion, anaphylaxis risk). Store protected from light.

indications.label: Iron Deficiency Anemia Prevention/Treatment
indications.note: AUDIT: Prophylaxis: 1-2mg/kg/day. Treatment: 3-6mg/kg/day. Give with vitamin C for absorption; avoid with milk/antacids. Stains teeth—use dropper to back of mouth.
